PR title: fix(nudge): add a drop verb for stale pending nudges instead of requiring manual state.json surgery (#5816)

PR description:
## What

#5816 (p2) has three asks. This addresses only the narrow, mechanical one: an operator CLI verb to drop a stale pending nudge, replacing manual `.gc/nudges/state.json` surgery. The other two — auto-detecting an epoch-superseded nudge against a continuously-busy target (the existing fence check only runs inside the delivery-attempt path, which requires session idleness, so it never fires against a busy session), and a TTL/expiry policy — are genuine design decisions (what's a "safe" wait, configurable or not, drop-vs-redeliver-as-default) and are explicitly not addressed here.

## Fix

`gc nudge drop <id>...` (matches the existing `gc mail delete <id>...` multi-ID convention), `--json` supported. Classifies each ID against current queue state, then calls the existing `recordQueuedNudgeFailureWithStore`/`failedQueuedNudge` dead-letter path in one batch — the same machinery `status`/`drain` already exercise internally on a real delivery failure, so a dropped nudge lands in the identical terminal state. No new state-machine logic.

One implementation detail: `failedQueuedNudge` only forces *immediate* dead-letter (vs. requeue-with-retry-delay) for a cause satisfying `errors.Is(cause, errNudgeSessionFenceMismatch)`. Rather than touching that function's branching, the new drop cause implements the standard `Is(target error) bool` method to report equivalence to that sentinel — idiomatic `errors.Is` usage, `failedQueuedNudge` itself is untouched, and the stored `LastError` text still reads "dropped by operator (gc nudge drop)" rather than borrowing the fence-mismatch sentinel's own message.

Per-ID outcomes are distinguished (droppable → dead-lettered, already-dead → clear no-op, not-found → clear error) and a batch with mixed valid/invalid IDs still processes the valid ones.

## Follow-up fixes included in this PR

The full local push-gate run surfaced two completeness gaps a narrower `cmd/gc`-only test pass had missed, both mechanical staleness rather than design decisions:

- **Product-metrics command census**: the new `gc nudge drop` command wasn't registered in `cmd/gc/productmetrics_command_census.json`, so `TestProductMetricsCommandCensusMatchesProductionBuiltins` failed with `live command "gc nudge drop" is missing` — which cascaded into ~30 other product-metrics classification/lifecycle tests that share the census as a precondition. Fixed by adding a manifest entry mirroring the sibling `gc nudge status` entry, then regenerating the derived artifacts via `go run ./cmd/gen-command-census`.
- **Two stale literals surfaced only by the census fix**: `test/packlint`'s deprecated-nudge-form doc-linter flagged the new auto-generated `gc nudge drop <id>... [flags]` docs line because its subcommand allowlist only knew `drain`/`status`/`poll` (added `drop`); `internal/productmetrics`'s `TestInjectedImmutableCommandCatalog...` asserted a hardcoded catalog-entry count (201) that grew to 202 once the new command's ID landed (updated the literal).

## Validation

- `go build -tags gms_pure_go ./...` clean, `gofmt -l .` empty
- `go test -tags gms_pure_go ./cmd/gc/... -run 'TestNudge|TestCmdNudge'` — all pass including 5 new tests
- `go test -tags gms_pure_go ./internal/productmetrics/... ./test/packlint/...` — pass
- `go run ./cmd/gen-command-census --check` passes
- Full local push-gate run (x4 across this session as fixes landed): final run's only failures are pre-existing environmental/timing flakes (dolt subprocess timing family in `examples/bd/dolt/`, systemctl-delegate/detached-probe/lsof tests, interrupt-timing tests in `internal/worker/adapters/zcode`) — confirmed via source lookup none touch `cmd_nudge.go` or any census file, and zero cascade failures across product-metrics/packlint
- Pre-commit lint clean (0 issues) on all three commits
